_meta.indication: Treatment of patients 6 months of age and older with relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma (LGG) harboring a BRAF fusion or rearrangement, or BRAF V600 mutation; approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and duration of response

pivotal_trials.population: Patients 6 months to 25 years of age with relapsed or refractory pediatric LGG harboring an activating BRAF alteration, required to have received at least one prior systemic therapy and documented radiographic progression
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) — defined as CR, PR, or MR — by independent review per RAPNO-LGG criteria
pivotal_trials.n: 76 patients (efficacy population; Table 10 efficacy results based on Arm-1)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 51% (95% CI: 40, 63) per RAPNO-LGG, with 28 partial responses (37%) and 11 minor responses (14%); median duration of response 13.8 months (95% CI: 11.3, NE)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) in FIREFLY-1 included rash (77%, Grade 3/4 12%), hair color changes (76%), fatigue (55%), viral infection (55%), vomiting (50%), headache (45%), and hemorrhage (42%, including one Grade 5 event). Hemorrhage, including intracranial hemorrhage, is a key risk — intracranial hemorrhage occurred at a rate of 11% in the target population including a Grade 5 event.
target_moa: Tovorafenib is an oral, CNS-penetrant Type II RAF kinase inhibitor of mutant BRAF V600E, wild-type BRAF, and wild-type CRAF kinases
companion_dx_detail: No FDA-approved companion diagnostic was available at approval; in FIREFLY-1 RAF alteration was determined by local molecular assays at CLIA or similarly certified laboratories. A PMC (4626-11) was issued to support development of an in vitro diagnostic device for BRAF fusion/rearrangement or BRAF V600 mutation.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected in the intended population

description.text: Updated labeling based on efficacy data from FIREFLY-1 and referenced an FDA-approved companion diagnostic

citations.quote: Prior Approval sNDA 002 provides for updates to the U.S. Prescribing Information (USPI) and Patient Information labeling, based on safety and efficacy data generated from Study DAY101-001/PNOC026 (FIREFLY-1); references the availability of an FDA-approved companion diagnostic; and provides for minor updates to the Instructions For Use labeling.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response — an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and duration of response [*see Clinical Studies (14)*].
The submitted evidence meets the statutory evidentiary standard for accelerated approval through demonstration of an effect on an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

basis.text: FDA granted breakthrough therapy designation to DAY101 (tovorafenib) for pediatric patients with LGG harboring an activating RAF alteration that have progressed after one or more prior systemic therapies, based on Study PNOC014 data

citations.quote: The FDA subsequently granted BTD to DAY101 for the treatment of pediatric patients with LGG harboring an activating RAF alteration that have progressed after one or more prior systemic therapies.

The BTDR was based on clinical data from Study PNOC014, an ongoing multicenter dose-escalation trial of DAY101 in patients 1 to 25 years of age with recurrent or progressive non-hematologic malignancies including CNS tumors, with a genomic mutation resulting in the activation of the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathway.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation for tovorafenib for the treatment of malignant glioma

citations.quote: Because the Applicant obtained orphan designation for tovorafenib for the treatment of malignant glioma, the application is exempt from PREA requirements.

summary.text: Tovorafenib (OJEMDA) received accelerated approval based on the large-magnitude, durable ORR and duration of response in the single-arm FIREFLY-1 trial, as an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. It was granted Priority review and breakthrough therapy designation, and holds orphan designation for malignant glioma. Continued approval is contingent on a confirmatory randomized trial (PMR 4626-1) versus physician's choice of chemotherapy.

requirement.text: 4626-10: Conduct a clinical PK trial with a strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducer to evaluate its effect on tovorafenib exposure and provide dosage recommendations for concomitant use with CYP2C8 inducers

citations.quote: 4626-10 Conduct a clinical pharmacokinetic trial with a strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducer with tovorafenib to evaluate the effect of a strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducer on decreasing the systemic exposure of tovorafenib and provide dosage recommendations for tovorafenib when used concomitantly with CYP2C8 inducers.

requirement.text: 4626-11: Conduct an analytical and clinical validation study to support development of an in vitro diagnostic device essential to the safe and effective use of tovorafenib for patients with LGG harboring a BRAF fusion/rearrangement or BRAF V600 mutation

citations.quote: 4626-11 Conduct an appropriate analytical and clinical validation study to support the development of an in vitro diagnostic device using clinical trial data that demonstrates that the device is essential to the safe and effective use of tovorafenib for the treatment of patients 6 months of age and older with relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma harboring a BRAF fusion or rearrangement, or BRAF V600 mutation.

requirement.text: 4626-12: Submit additional dissolution profile data using the final dissolution method for three commercial batches of Tovorafenib Powder for Oral Suspension, 25 mg/mL

citations.quote: 4626-12 Submission of additional dissolution profile data using the final dissolution method (USP apparatus II, 50 rpm, 900 mL 0.1 N HCl with 0.3% SDS) for three commercial batches of Tovorafenib Powder for Oral Suspension, 25 mg/mL to finalize the drug product acceptance criterion for the dissolution test and support the proposed expiry date/shelf life.
